shot1: Shot 1 opens directly with a close-up overhead composition, featuring a baseplate, door frame, window, roof piece, small tree, and streetlight arranged centrally on the table. Sorted building blocks form clear leading lines along the left and right sides of the frame. In the foreground, a pair of hands is poised to begin assembling. The background is softly blurred, revealing warm-toned storage cabinets and a corner of a bed in a child's room. The lighting is soft and even. The camera performs an extremely subtle push-in, emphasizing the neat and orderly arrangement of materials.
shot2: The second shot cuts abruptly from the previous one, transitioning to a medium close-up overhead view. The baseplate is brought from the left side of the frame to the center, with the composition centered on the baseplate and ample negative space around it to clearly observe its outline. Warm lighting creates soft highlights along the edges of the baseplate. As the child places the baseplate flat, they say “先拿出底板，确定小房子的范围”, and when reaching “范围”, their finger slowly traces around the edge of the baseplate. The The camera slightly tilts downward to follow the hand motion, clearly establishing the foundational area.
shot3: Shot 3 cuts abruptly from the previous shot, using a close-up overhead view. The four corners occupy the four visual focal points of the frame, with shallow depth of field making the grid lines on the baseplate and the corner foundation blocks clearer. A child's hands sequentially place each of the four foundation blocks onto the corners, while narrating “接着把四角先固定，这样后面更稳”. The lighting remains warm and clean, and the camera performs subtle lateral movements, following the installation process at each of the four corners in turn.
shot4: Shot 4 continues with a hard cut from the previous shot, transitioning to a medium shot with a slightly high-angle to eye-level perspective. The tabletop and baseboard create a clear foreground-background layering, while the building blocks extend upward in successive layers from bottom to top. The background of the children's room remains softly blurred to maintain continuity. A crisp, rhythmic tapping The camera slowly pans and slightly pushes in, helping viewers clearly observe the progressive development of the wall structure.
shot5: Shot 5 cuts directly from the previous shot, using a close-up at eye level with a slight downward angle. The camera height is lowered to the side of the wall, embedding the door frame and window into the action for greater depth. In the foreground are unassembled window and door components, with focus on the opening in the midground wall. Warm light sweeps across the plastic surface from the right, creating delicate reflections. The shape change and precise placement of the component are clearly visible. The camera gently shifts sideways and slightly pushes in, emphasizing accurate alignment.
shot6: Shot 6 cuts abruptly from the previous shot, transitioning to a medium close-up overhead view. The house structure is now more complete, with noticeably fewer blocks remaining around it, creating a sense of time progression. The child's hands continue building upward on the wall and deliberately leave a flat, open space on one side while explaining “继续往上搭，但是这里要空出来做二层平台”. When mentioning “空出来”, the child briefly pauses their hand motion to indicate the empty area, then resumes placing blocks around it. The lighting remains warm and steady, and the camera performs a slight circular dolly movement, allowing the reserved platform space to be clearly visible from multiple angles.
shot7: Shot 7 cuts directly from the previous shot, using a close-up at eye level, with the focus on the staircase and balcony components. shot8: Shot 8 cuts hard from the previous shot, transitioning to a close-up overhead angle slightly from the front. The roof piece enters the frame from the top, with the main house structure centered. The background depth of field is shallower to emphasize the final assembly of the large component. Warm light creates a soft highlight along the edge of the roof. The camera performs a short push-in, intensifying the moment the structure is completed.
shot9: Shot 9 cuts abruptly from the previous shot, using a medium close-up overhead view. The complete house is now fully formed, with small trees and streetlights placed symmetrically on either side of the foreground as decorative elements, creating a more balanced composition. The camera slowly pulls back slightly, allowing both the decoration and inspection actions to be clearly visible.
shot10: Shot 10 transitions from the previous shot with a subtle fade-in/fade-out, cutting to a wide eye-level view. The completed small house is centered on the tabletop, with a child in the foreground gently turning the finished model toward the camera. The warm-toned children's room environment in the background is fully visible, creating a bright, satisfying, and cozy atmosphere.
